rationale: M60 R10 — the java override-KEY class, found by the target-spelling census (validation/m60/target-spelling-register.json) and root-caused in grails-core: an override endpoint is built as `${ownerFqn}.${name}${signature}`, so the label comes from splitting a string that CONTAINS a parameter list, and the pre-fix rule (split on '.', last two segments, cut each at '(') split the parameter list itself whenever a parameter TYPE was written with a dot. Two live shapes are pinned here: a QUALIFIED parameter type in a non-final position (grails JpaQueryBuilder.java, 84 mangled sides on a 300-file draw — `handle.Criterion,StringBuilder,…boolean)`) and a GENERIC parameter type (`Map.Entry<String, Boolean>`, the GrailsResourceUtils.java `removeEldestEntry` shape). The parameter types are written qualified on purpose: the signature carries the WRITTEN text, so an unqualified `Criterion` would not exercise the class at all. The third shape (dotted type in the LAST position) is the same rule reached from the other side — it makes the last-two window shift rather than the method name survive.

forbidRelationships.note: pre-fix: the parameter list's dot (Outer.Criterion) was split as a qualifier, so BOTH sides of the edge were this string — no name, and the owner class lost. Measured on grails-core JpaQueryBuilder.java.
pre-fix: a GENERIC parameter type shifts the last-two window and leaves an unbalanced ')' — the GrailsResourceUtils.java shape, where the honest key is LinkedHashMap.removeEldestEntry.
